item.research_question: How do AlxCoCrFeNi high entropy alloys behave under ion irradiation, specifically in terms of precipitation?
item.processing_route: Arc-melting and drop-casting, with subsequent polishing and preparation for TEM analysis
item.test_conditions: Irradiation with 3 MeV Au ions at room temperature, with fluences ranging from 1 × 10^14 to 1 × 10^16 cm^-2
item.mechanism: The high configurational entropy and low atomic mobility of single-phase HEAs reduce the thermodynamic driving force and kinetically restrain the formation of precipitates, respectively
item.limitations: The study only investigates the irradiation responses of HEAs at room temperature, and further studies are needed to understand their behavior at elevated temperatures
item.future_work: Systematic studies on the irradiation responses of HEAs at elevated temperatures are required for their applications in advanced nuclear systems
quotes: the high configurational entropy and low atomic mobility
the great structure stability of single phase HEA against precipitation under ion irradiation

records.text: Paper card. Question: How do AlxCoCrFeNi high entropy alloys behave under ion irradiation, specifically in terms of precipitation?. System: AlxCoCrFeNi (x = 0.1, 0.75, and 1.5) high entropy alloys. Processing: Arc-melting and drop-casting, with subsequent polishing and preparation for TEM analysis. Test conditions: Irradiation with 3 MeV Au ions at room temperature, with fluences ranging from 1 × 10^14 to 1 × 10^16 cm^-2. Findings: 1.887e+16; 1.0; 8.1; 7.4; 6.9; 100; 40; 300000000000.0; 100000000000000.0; 1e+16; 43. Mechanism: The high configurational entropy and low atomic mobility of single-phase HEAs reduce the thermodynamic driving force and kinetically restrain the formation of precipitates, respectively. Limitations: The study only investigates the irradiation responses of HEAs at room temperature, and further studies are needed to understand their behavior at elevated temperatures. Future work: Systematic studies on the irradiation responses of HEAs at elevated temperatures are required for their applications in advanced nuclear systems.
